blocks.text: A Shared Question — The Practice After Class
Era Zero, during the Great Flourishing. New song-cycle fiction at the Central House of Meaning, before the Era One events of The First Silenced Chord.

At the Central House of Meaning, Pelli stayed after a language exercise to practice with two classmates. Each could hold a different part of the lesson comfortably. Pelli could keep a clear, ringing line, but lost their place whenever they tried to listen and improve it at the same time.

They began again with shorter statements about inquiry, attention and shared understanding. One classmate answered with a reception phrase; the other sang a statement about their shared channel. When Pelli stopped, neither filled the silence for them.

The exercise became A Shared Question. Its title named what the classmates were doing together. The language phrases in this arrangement remain assertions; the title does not silently turn them into interrogatives.

The three performed it once for the caretaker closing their practice area. The caretaker listened, thanked them, and asked them to put the cushions away. Pelli liked that ending enough to keep it: the music could matter without becoming an examination or a famous Work.

Pelli and both classmates sing complete Era Zero statements. Pelli leads with attention and expression phrases; the first classmate answers with reception and shared attention; the second supports them with phrases about a shared channel and enduring attentional capacity. Each voice can be heard alone. Their overlapping parts carry no environmental execution channel.

The Central House and its teaching architecture are established in The First Silenced Chord. Pelli and the classmates are new Era Zero figures, not replacements for Talar, Nemi or their later students. That story is a later connection, not an event these performers witnessed.
